quizName: DMV Practice Test #10 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: Under normal conditions, a motorcyclist should stay at least how far behind the vehicle ahead?
questions.explanation: Motorcyclists should keep at least a two-second distance from the vehicle ahead in normal conditions. In bad weather or poor road conditions, you should increase this distance.

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT help reduce crash risk?

options.text: Be ready to react to hazards.
Turn your headlight off during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your headlight off during the day.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, stay visible to other drivers. Use your signals, brake lights, and proper lane position. Keep space around your motorcycle and always watch the road ahead, behind, and beside you.

questions.question: A person with a blood alcohol content (BAC) of ____ or higher is considered intoxicated.
questions.explanation: In Virginia, a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher means a person is intoxicated. Intoxicated people cannot legally operate a motor vehicle.

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT help you control a motorcycle while turning?
questions.explanation: To control a motorcycle in a turn, slow down before you turn. Look where you want to go, lean the motorcycle, and then gently roll on the throttle while turning to keep the suspension stable.

questions.question: A motorized scooter can be operated:

options.text: With any class of driver license.

questions.correctAnswerText: With any class of driver license.
questions.explanation: In California, anyone with any type of driver license can operate a motorized scooter.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. This sign warns that the road may be slippery when wet.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign is placed on slow-moving vehicles going under 25 mph, like farm equipment, construction vehicles, or horse-drawn wagons.

questions.question: You should flash your brake light to:

options.text: Alert other drivers that you are nearby.
Help other drivers see your motorcycle in slow traffic.
Warn drivers you are slowing down or stopping when they don't expect it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Warn drivers you are slowing down or stopping when they don't expect it.
questions.explanation: Use your brake light to communicate with other drivers. Flash it before making a quick, tight turn off a high-speed road or whenever you slow down in a place where drivers may not expect it.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. This sign warns that traffic ahead will merge together.

questions.question: The body removes alcohol at a rate of approximately:
questions.explanation: The body removes about one drink per hour on average. This rate varies by person. The safest choice is to never ride after drinking any alcohol.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT recommended as protective gear for motorcycle riders?
questions.explanation: When riding a motorcycle, wear protective gear. Good protective clothing includes long-sleeved jackets, long heavy pants, closed-toe boots that cover your ankles, and full-fingered leather gloves. Cover as much skin as possible when riding.

questions.question: When choosing a jacket for protection, it should:

options.text: Fit loosely and flap in the wind.
Fit snugly so it does not flap in the wind.
Not be made of leather or another sturdy material.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fit snugly so it does not flap in the wind.
questions.explanation: Choose pants and a jacket made of leather or another sturdy material. They should fit snugly so they do not flap in the wind, but loose enough that you can move freely.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, you should:
questions.explanation: Gloves improve your grip and protect your hands while riding. Wear gloves that cover all your fingers and are made of durable material.

questions.question: The Motorcycle Safety Foundation recommends the SEE strategy for safe riding. What does SEE stand for?
questions.explanation: Experienced riders use the SEE strategy to make safe decisions. SEE stands for Search, Evaluate, and Execute.

questions.question: How should you brake on a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: When making a normal stop on a motorcycle:

options.text: Apply the front and rear brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Apply the front and rear brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: For a normal stop, use the front and rear brakes at the same time and downshift.

questions.question: You should not ride directly next to another vehicle because:

options.text: The other driver may want to use your lane to pass.
You may be in the vehicle's blind spot.
You may have access to escape routes.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may be in the vehicle's blind spot.
questions.explanation: Riding next to another vehicle is dangerous because you may be in its blind spot. The driver will not see you. Also, the vehicle may block your escape route if a hazard appears.

questions.question: If your front wheel locks while braking, you should:

options.text: Keep the tire locked to stop more quickly.
Release the front brake and use only the rear brake.
Release the front brake and re-apply it right away.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake and re-apply it right away.
questions.explanation: If the front wheel locks up while braking, release the front brake pressure immediately. Then re-apply pressure to the brake gradually and in a controlled way.

questions.question: Most motorcycle and car accidents happen:
questions.explanation: Most collisions between motorcycles and cars happen at intersections. The most common cause is the car driver failing to yield the right-of-way to the motorcycle rider.

questions.question: When riding near a truck:

options.text: If you cannot see the truck's mirrors, the driver cannot see you.
You should not be able to see the truck's mirrors.
Focus on riding and do not worry about the truck's mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: If you cannot see the truck's mirrors, the driver cannot see you.
questions.explanation: Avoid staying in the blind spots of any vehicle, especially large trucks. Remember: if you cannot see the truck's mirrors, the driver cannot see you.

questions.question: When braking on a motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Apply the front and rear brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Apply the front and rear brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop. Using only the rear brake may prevent you from learning to use the front brake correctly when you need to stop quickly.

questions.question: When should you increase your following distance?
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when your motorcycle takes longer to stop than normal, when you cannot see through the vehicle ahead, or when traffic is heavy and other vehicles may try to cut in front of you.

questions.question: What is true about motorcycle mirrors?

options.text: The mirrors show everything around you.
The mirrors do not show your blind spots.
You should only use mirrors when parking.

questions.correctAnswerText: The mirrors do not show your blind spots.
questions.explanation: Motorcycle mirrors have blind spots, just like any other vehicle. Always turn your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: What does an integrated braking system do?

options.text: It connects the front and rear brakes together when you use the rear brake.
It automatically applies the brakes based on your riding habits.
It applies the brake when you downshift.

questions.correctAnswerText: It connects the front and rear brakes together when you use the rear brake.
questions.explanation: Some motorcycles have integrated braking systems that connect the front and rear brakes when the rider applies the rear brake pedal. Check your owner's manual to learn about your motorcycle's braking system.

questions.question: If your front tire goes flat, your steering will feel:
questions.explanation: If your steering suddenly feels heavy, your front tire may be flat. Stop riding and check your tires right away.
